sentences.zh: 志一百五

translations.literal: Treatise 105.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 105

sentences.zh: 兵一

translations.literal: Military Affairs 1.
translations.idiomatic: Military Affairs, Part One

sentences.zh: 有清以武功定天下。

translations.literal: The Qing, by martial achievement, settled the realm under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing dynasty secured rule over the empire through military prowess.

sentences.zh: 太祖高皇帝崛起東方，初定旗兵制，八旗子弟人盡為兵，不啻舉國皆兵焉。

translations.literal: The Great Founder rose in the east, first established the banner-soldier system; among the Eight Banners every clansman became a soldier—it was as if the whole nation were an army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Founder Taizu rose in the east, he first established the banner army system: every man of the Eight Banners was a soldier, so that the state was, in effect, a nation in arms.

sentences.zh: 太宗征籓部，世祖定中原，八旗兵力最強。

translations.literal: Taizong campaigned against the frontier tribes; Shizu settled the Central Plains—the Eight Banners' military strength was at its peak.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong, who campaigned against the frontier peoples, and Shunzhi, who secured the Central Plains, the fighting power of the Eight Banners reached its height.

sentences.zh: 聖祖平南服，世宗征青海，高宗定西疆，以旗兵為主，而輔之以綠營。

translations.literal: Shengzu pacified the southern regions; Shizong campaigned in Qinghai; Gaozong settled the western frontier—banner troops served as the main force, assisted by the Green Standard Army.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi pacified the south, Yongzheng campaigned in Qinghai, and Qianlong secured the western borderlands, relying chiefly on banner forces supplemented by the Green Standard Army.

sentences.zh: 仁宗剿教匪，宣宗御外寇，兼用防軍，而以鄉兵助之。

translations.literal: Renzong suppressed the sect rebels; Xuanzong repelled foreign invaders—both employed garrison troops together, with local militia to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaqing suppressed the sectarian rebels and Daoguang met foreign incursions by employing garrison forces as well, aided by local militia.

sentences.zh: 文宗、穆宗先後平粵、捻，湘軍初起，淮軍繼之，而練勇之功始著，至是兵制蓋數變矣。

translations.literal: Wenzong and Muzong in succession pacified the Cantonese and Nian rebels; the Xiang Army arose first, the Huai Army followed, and the achievements of trained braves first became notable—by then the military system had changed several times.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianfeng and Tongzhi the Taiping and Nian rebellions were suppressed in turn: the Hunan Army was raised first, the Anhui Army followed, and the trained militia corps first proved their worth—by this point the army system had undergone several transformations.

sentences.zh: 道、咸以後，海禁大開，德宗復立海軍，內江外海，與水師並行。

translations.literal: After the Daoguang and Xianfeng reigns, maritime prohibitions were greatly relaxed; Dezong again established a navy—on inland rivers and the open sea, operating alongside the water forces.
translations.idiomatic: After the Daoguang and Xianfeng eras the maritime frontier opened wide; Guangxu re-established a navy, and forces on inland rivers and the open sea operated alongside the water divisions.

sentences.zh: 而練軍、陸軍又相繼以起，擾攘數年，卒釀新軍之變。

translations.literal: Then trained armies and land forces arose in succession; after years of turmoil, they finally brought about the New Army uprising.
translations.idiomatic: Trained corps and land armies were raised in turn; after years of unrest they culminated in the New Army mutiny.

sentences.zh: 以兵興者，終以兵敗。

translations.literal: What rose by the sword, in the end fell by the sword.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty that rose by force of arms was ultimately undone by force of arms.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，豈非天哉！

translations.literal: Alas—is this not Heaven's will!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—was this not the decree of Heaven!

sentences.zh: 今作兵志：一曰八旗，二曰綠營，三曰防軍，附陸軍，四曰鄉兵，五曰土兵，六曰水師，七曰海軍，八曰邊防，九曰海防，十曰訓練，十一曰製造，十二曰馬政，並分著於篇。

translations.literal: Now this Military Treatise is composed: first, the Eight Banners; second, the Green Standard Army; third, garrison troops, with land forces appended; fourth, local militia; fifth, native troops; sixth, the water forces; seventh, the navy; eighth, frontier defense; ninth, coastal defense; tenth, training; eleventh, manufacture; twelfth, horse administration—all set forth in separate sections.
translations.idiomatic: This Military Treatise is organized as follows: (1) the Eight Banners; (2) the Green Standard Army; (3) garrison troops, with land forces treated alongside; (4) local militia; (5) native levies; (6) the water forces; (7) the navy; (8) frontier defense; (9) coastal defense; (10) training; (11) arms manufacture; and (12) horse administration—each treated in its own section.

sentences.zh: 八旗

translations.literal: The Eight Banners.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Banners

sentences.zh: 清初，太祖以遺甲十三副起，歸附日眾，設四旗，曰正黃、正白、正紅、正藍，復增四旗，曰鑲黃、鑲白、鑲紅、鑲藍，統滿洲、蒙古、漢軍之眾，八旗之制自此始。

translations.literal: In the early Qing, the Founder rose with thirteen suits of inherited armor; those who submitted grew daily. He established four banners—Plain Yellow, Plain White, Plain Red, and Plain Blue—and added four more: Bordered Yellow, Bordered White, Bordered Red, and Bordered Blue, commanding Manchu, Mongol, and Han Army forces—the Eight Banner system began here.
translations.idiomatic: In the founding years Taizu rose with thirteen suits of inherited armor; as followers flocked to him he first established four banners—Plain Yellow, White, Red, and Blue—then added four bordered banners, commanding Manchu, Mongol, and Han bannermen alike. Thus the Eight Banner system took shape.

sentences.zh: 每旗三百人為一牛錄，以牛錄額真領之。

translations.literal: Every three hundred men in a banner formed one niru, led by a niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Each banner unit of three hundred men formed a niru, commanded by a niru captain.

sentences.zh: 五牛錄，領以札蘭額真。

translations.literal: Five niru were led by a jalan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Five niru were grouped under a jalan commander.

sentences.zh: 五札蘭，領以固山額真。

translations.literal: Five jalan were led by a gushan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Five jalan formed a banner under a gushan commander.

sentences.zh: 每固山設左右梅勒額真。

translations.literal: Each gushan had left and right meiren ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Each banner had left and right deputy commanders (meiren ejen).

sentences.zh: 天命五年，改牛錄額真俱為備御官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianming, all niru ejen were changed to beiyu officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianming (1620) all niru captains were redesignated as defense officers.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，定八旗官名，總兵為昂邦章京，副將為梅勒章京，參將為甲喇章京，各分三等。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong, Eight Banner official titles were fixed: commander-in-chief was angbang janggin, deputy commander meiren janggin, brigade commander jalan janggin—each in three grades.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tiancong (1634) banner ranks were standardized: the commander-in-chief as angbang janggin, deputy as meiren janggin, and brigade leader as jalan janggin, each in three grades.

sentences.zh: 備御為牛錄章京。

translations.literal: Beiyu became niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: Defense officers were titled niru janggin.

sentences.zh: 什長為專達。

translations.literal: Squad leaders were called zhunda.
translations.idiomatic: Squad leaders were known as zhunda.

sentences.zh: 又定固山額真行營馬兵為阿禮哈超哈，其後曰驍騎營。

translations.literal: It was further fixed that gushan ejen field-camp cavalry were alihaha caha, later called the Vanguard Cavalry Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: Banner field cavalry were designated alihaha caha, later known as the Vanguard Cavalry Brigade.

sentences.zh: 巴雅喇營前哨兵為噶布什賢超哈，其後曰護軍及前鋒營。

translations.literal: Bayara camp vanguard troops were gabushiha caha, later called the Guard Corps and Vanguard Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: Bayara camp scouts were gabushiha caha, later reorganized as the Guard Corps and Vanguard Brigade.

sentences.zh: 駐防盛京兵為守兵，預備兵為援兵。

translations.literal: Troops garrisoned at Mukden were guard troops; reserve troops were relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: Forces stationed at Mukden served as garrison troops; reserves served as relief troops.

sentences.zh: 各城寨兵為守邊兵。

translations.literal: Troops at each fortress and stockade were frontier-guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons at fortified towns and stockades served as frontier guards.

sentences.zh: 舊蒙古左右營為左右翼兵。

translations.literal: The former Mongol left and right camps became left- and right-wing troops.
translations.idiomatic: The former Mongol left and right camps became the left and right wings.

sentences.zh: 舊漢兵為烏真超哈。

translations.literal: Former Han troops were ujen caha.
translations.idiomatic: Former Han troops were organized as ujen caha (heavy artillery).

sentences.zh: 孔有德之天祐兵，尚可喜之天助兵，併入漢軍。

translations.literal: Kong Youde's Tianyou troops and Shang Kexi's Tianzhu troops were merged into the Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Youde's Tianyou corps and Shang Kexi's Tianzhu corps were incorporated into the Han banners.

sentences.zh: 九年，以所獲察哈爾部眾及喀喇沁壯丁分為蒙古八旗，制與滿洲八旗同。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Chahar tribesmen captured and Kharachin able-bodied men were divided into Mongol Eight Banners, with regulations identical to the Manchu Eight Banners.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1635) captured Chahar tribesmen and Kharachin levies were organized into eight Mongol banners on the same model as the Manchu banners.

sentences.zh: 崇德二年，分漢軍為二旗，置左右翼。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongde, the Han Army was divided into two banners, with left and right wings established.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chongde (1637) the Han banners were split into two, with left and right wings.

sentences.zh: 四年，分為四旗，曰純皁、曰皁鑲黃、曰皁鑲白、曰皁鑲紅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, they were divided into four banners: called Pure Black, Black-Bordered Yellow, Black-Bordered White, and Black-Bordered Red.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1639) they were further divided into four banners: Plain Black, Black-Bordered Yellow, Black-Bordered White, and Black-Bordered Red.

sentences.zh: 七年，設漢軍八旗，制與滿洲同。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Han Army Eight Banners were established, with regulations the same as the Manchu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1642) the full eight Han banners were established on the Manchu model.

sentences.zh: 世祖定鼎燕京，分置滿、蒙、漢八旗於京城。

translations.literal: Shizu established the capital at Yanjing and stationed Manchu, Mongol, and Han Eight Banners in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzhi made Beijing the capital, Manchu, Mongol, and Han banners were posted throughout the city.

sentences.zh: 以次釐定兵制。

translations.literal: Thereupon the military system was gradually regulated.
translations.idiomatic: The military establishment was then systematically codified.

sentences.zh: 禁衛兵大類有二：曰郎衛，曰兵衛。

translations.literal: Palace guard troops fall into two broad categories: called langwei and bingwei.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards fell into two broad categories: court attendants (langwei) and garrison guards (bingwei).

sentences.zh: 郎衛之制，領侍衛內大臣六人，鑲黃、正黃、正白旗各二人。

translations.literal: For the langwei system, six leading imperial bodyguard grand ministers were appointed—two each from the Bordered Yellow, Plain Yellow, and Plain White banners.
translations.idiomatic: Under the langwei system six grand ministers of the imperial bodyguard were appointed, two each from the Bordered Yellow, Plain Yellow, and Plain White banners.

sentences.zh: 內大臣六人。

translations.literal: Six inner grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: There were six inner grand ministers.

sentences.zh: 散秩大臣無定員。

translations.literal: Ministers without regular rank had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers of honorific rank had no fixed number.

sentences.zh: 侍衛分四等。

translations.literal: Bodyguards were divided into four grades.
translations.idiomatic: Bodyguards were ranked in four grades.

sentences.zh: 更有藍翎侍衛。

translations.literal: There were also blue-plume bodyguards.
translations.idiomatic: There were also blue-plume bodyguards.

sentences.zh: 凡御前侍衛、乾清門侍衛由三旗簡用，漢侍衛由武進士簡用，皆無定員。

translations.literal: All imperial-audience bodyguards and Qianqing Gate bodyguards were selected from the three banners; Han bodyguards were selected from military jinshi—all without fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial-audience and Qianqing Gate guards were drawn from the three upper banners; Han guards from military jinshi graduates—with no fixed quotas for any of them.

sentences.zh: 初，鑲黃、正黃、正白三旗，天子自將，選其子弟曰侍衛，凡值殿廷，以領侍衛內大臣統之。

translations.literal: At first the Bordered Yellow, Plain Yellow, and Plain White banners were personally commanded by the Son of Heaven; their young clansmen were selected as bodyguards. All who served in the palace halls were commanded by the leading imperial bodyguard grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the three upper banners were under the emperor's direct command; their young clansmen were chosen as bodyguards, and all who served in the palace halls were overseen by the grand ministers of the imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 宿衛乾清門、內右門、神武門、寧壽門為內班，宿衛太和門為外班。

translations.literal: Those who garrisoned the Qianqing Gate, Inner Right Gate, Divine Martial Gate, and Ningshou Gate were the inner watch; those who garrisoned the Gate of Supreme Harmony were the outer watch.
translations.idiomatic: Guards posted at the Qianqing, Inner Right, Divine Martial, and Ningshou gates formed the inner watch; those at the Gate of Supreme Harmony formed the outer watch.

sentences.zh: 行幸駐蹕咸從。

translations.literal: On imperial tours and encampments, all followed in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial progresses and encampments they all accompanied the throne.

sentences.zh: 其扈從，後扈二人，前引十人，豹尾班侍衛六十人。

translations.literal: Their escort comprised two rear guards, ten forward guides, and sixty bodyguards of the Leopard-Tail Company.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial escort comprised two rear guards, ten forward guides, and sixty bodyguards of the Leopard-Tail Company.

sentences.zh: 凡佐領親軍，鑲黃旗滿洲八十五佐領，蒙古二十八佐領，每佐領親軍二人；

translations.literal: As for company-commander personal guards: the Bordered Yellow Manchu banner had eighty-five companies, Mongol twenty-eight companies—two personal guards per company;
translations.idiomatic: Personal guards attached to company officers: the Bordered Yellow banner had eighty-five Manchu and twenty-eight Mongol companies, each contributing two personal guards;

sentences.zh: 正黃旗滿洲九十三佐領，蒙古二十四佐領；

translations.literal: the Plain Yellow Manchu ninety-three companies, Mongol twenty-four companies;
translations.idiomatic: the Plain Yellow banner had ninety-three Manchu and twenty-four Mongol companies;

sentences.zh: 正白旗滿洲八十六佐領，蒙古二十九佐領。

translations.literal: the Plain White Manchu eighty-six companies, Mongol twenty-nine companies.
translations.idiomatic: the Plain White banner had eighty-six Manchu and twenty-nine Mongol companies.

sentences.zh: 三旗親軍選六十人隨侍衛行走，餘皆值宿。

translations.literal: From the three banners' personal guards, sixty were chosen to march with the bodyguards; the rest all stood night watch.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty personal guards from the three banners marched with the bodyguard corps; the remainder stood regular watch duty.

sentences.zh: 巡幸則御前大臣侍衛、乾清門侍衛咸從。

translations.literal: On tours of inspection, imperial-audience grand minister bodyguards and Qianqing Gate bodyguards all followed.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours both the grand minister bodyguards and the Qianqing Gate guards accompanied the throne.

sentences.zh: 行營則列兩廂，餘於幔城之隅，環拱宿衛。

translations.literal: In field camps they were arrayed in the two wings; the rest at the corners of the tent enclosure, encircling in guard watch.
translations.idiomatic: In field camps they were posted in the two wings; the remainder ringed the tent enclosure on night watch.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十九年，以武進士技優者拔置侍衛，偕三旗值宿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi, military jinshi of superior skill were selected and appointed bodyguards, standing watch together with the three banners.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi (1690) skilled military jinshi were promoted to bodyguards and posted on watch alongside the three banners.

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年，以親軍未滿十年者，挑選前鋒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng, personal guards who had not yet served ten years were selected for the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng (1733) personal guards with less than ten years' service were drafted into the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 滿、漢八旗左右翼各設前鋒統領一人，備警蹕宿衛。

translations.literal: For Manchu and Han Eight Banners, left and right wings each had one vanguard commander, to provide escort alert and night guard.
translations.idiomatic: Each wing of the Manchu and Han banners had a vanguard commander responsible for escort security and palace watch.

sentences.zh: 侍衛班內有上駟院侍衛，司轡、司鞍。

translations.literal: Within the bodyguard corps were Imperial Stud bodyguards, who managed bridles and saddles.
translations.idiomatic: The bodyguard corps included Imperial Stud guards in charge of bridles and saddles.

sentences.zh: 其兼尚虞、鷹鷂房、鶻房、十五善射、射鵠、善撲等侍衛，統在三旗額內，俱無定員。

translations.literal: Those who also served in the Imperial Hunt, Falconry, Gyrfalcon, Fifteen-Skill Archery, Swan-Shooting, and Wrestling offices—all counted within the three-banner quota, all without fixed numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Bodyguards who also served the Imperial Hunt, Falconry, Gyrfalcon Office, Fifteen-Skill Archery, Swan-Shooting, and Wrestling bureaus were all drawn from the three-banner quota, with no fixed numbers.

sentences.zh: 鑾儀衛亦侍從武職。

translations.literal: The Imperial Procession Guard were also attendant military offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Procession Guard were also martial attendants of the court.

sentences.zh: 設掌衛司內大臣一人，鑾儀使三人，冠軍使十人，雲麾使、治儀正、整儀尉各有差，專司乘輿鹵簿。

translations.literal: One inner grand minister of the Guard Bureau was appointed; three procession commissioners, ten champion commissioners, cloud-banner commissioners, ritual rectifiers, and formation marshals in varying numbers—all exclusively managing the imperial carriage and regalia.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau had one inner grand minister, three procession commissioners, ten champion commissioners, and various cloud-banner commissioners, ritual rectifiers, and formation marshals, all charged with the imperial carriage and ceremonial regalia.

sentences.zh: 校尉由內府選者為旗尉，由五城選者為民尉。

translations.literal: Sergeants selected by the Imperial Household were banner sergeants; those selected by the Five Cities were civilian sergeants.
translations.idiomatic: Sergeants chosen by the Imperial Household were banner sergeants; those chosen by the Five Cities were civilian sergeants.

sentences.zh: 此八旗郎衛制也。

translations.literal: This was the Eight Banner langwei system.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the Eight Banner langwei (court guard) establishment.

sentences.zh: 兵衛之制，定鼎初，即以上三旗守衛紫禁宮闕，以護軍統領、參領、前鋒統領率之。

translations.literal: For the bingwei system: at the founding of the capital, the three upper banners immediately guarded the Forbidden City palaces, led by guard commanders, brigade commanders, and vanguard commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Under the bingwei system, from the founding of the capital the three upper banners guarded the Forbidden City, commanded by guard corps leaders, brigade officers, and vanguard commanders.

sentences.zh: 噶布什賢超哈滿洲、蒙古八旗分左右翼備宿衛。

translations.literal: Gabushiha caha of the Manchu and Mongol Eight Banners were divided into left and right wings for night guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: Gabushiha scouts of the Manchu and Mongol banners were organized in left and right wings for palace night watch.

sentences.zh: 內務府三旗，各設佐領三人，旗鼓佐領四人，正黃旗設朝鮮佐領一人，每二丁設馬甲一，每佐領各設領催六、護軍十五，以領侍衛內大臣率之。

translations.literal: The Imperial Household's three banners each had three company commanders, four banner-and-drum company commanders; the Plain Yellow banner had one Korean company commander. For every two men one armored soldier was assigned; each company had six squad leaders and fifteen guards—all led by the leading imperial bodyguard grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Household's three banners each had three company officers and four banner-and-drum officers; the Plain Yellow banner also had a Korean company. One armored soldier was assigned per two men; each company had six squad leaders and fifteen guards, all under the grand ministers of the imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 內務府官兵守護行宮者，分東西北三路，設千總等官、兵額不等。

translations.literal: Imperial Household troops guarding traveling palaces were divided into east, north, and west routes, with battalion commanders and other officers appointed—troop quotas varying.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Household troops assigned to traveling palaces were divided into eastern, northern, and western routes, with battalion commanders and varying troop strengths.

sentences.zh: 熱河行宮亦如之。

translations.literal: The Rehe traveling palace was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Rehe traveling palace followed the same arrangement.

sentences.zh: 其守護陵寢者，順治初，永陵、福陵、昭陵各設雲騎尉、騎都尉。

translations.literal: Those who guarded the mausoleums: in the early Shunzhi reign, at the Yongling, Fuling, and Zhaoling tombs, cloud-cavalry commandants and cavalry commandants were each established.
translations.idiomatic: Guards for the imperial tombs: in early Shunzhi, the Yongling, Fuling, and Zhaoling mausoleums each had cloud-cavalry and cavalry commandants appointed.

sentences.zh: 嗣後盛京三陵，增設總管、防禦、驍騎校。

translations.literal: Later at the three Mukden mausoleums, superintendents, defense officers, and vanguard cavalry captains were added.
translations.idiomatic: Later superintendents, defense officers, and vanguard cavalry captains were added at the three Mukden tombs.

sentences.zh: 京師東西陵制亦如之。

translations.literal: The regulations for the eastern and western mausoleums near the capital were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern and western mausoleums near Beijing followed the same system.

sentences.zh: 所屬各旗驍騎有差。

translations.literal: The vanguard cavalry attached to each banner varied in number.
translations.idiomatic: Attached vanguard cavalry from the various banners varied in strength.

sentences.zh: 八年，制定親王至輔國公等，以次設長史、護衛等官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, regulations were fixed for princes down to bulwark dukes, establishing in order chancellors, guards, and other officers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1651) ranks from prince down to bulwark duke were each assigned chancellors, guards, and other officers in due order.

sentences.zh: 十七年，定八旗漢字官名，固山額真曰都統，梅勒章京曰副都統，甲喇章京曰參領，牛錄章京曰佐領，昂邦章京曰總管，烏真超哈曰漢軍。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Eight Banner Chinese official titles were fixed: gushan ejen became commander-in-chief, meiren janggin deputy commander-in-chief, jalan janggin brigade commander, niru janggin company commander, angbang janggin superintendent, ujen caha Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1660) Chinese titles for banner offices were standardized: gushan ejen as banner commander, meiren janggin as deputy commander, jalan janggin as brigade leader, niru janggin as company officer, angbang janggin as superintendent, and ujen caha as the Han Army.

sentences.zh: 凡滿、蒙、漢各旗共選四千八百人為養育兵，訓練技藝。

translations.literal: In all, from Manchu, Mongol, and Han banners, four thousand eight hundred men were selected as nurture-soldiers to train in skills.
translations.idiomatic: Four thousand eight hundred men were selected from the Manchu, Mongol, and Han banners as nurture-soldiers for skills training.

sentences.zh: 嗣後兵額屢增。

translations.literal: Thereafter troop quotas were repeatedly increased.
translations.idiomatic: Troop quotas were increased repeatedly thereafter.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，滿、蒙養育兵至二萬三百餘人。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong period, Manchu and Mongol nurture-soldiers reached more than twenty thousand three hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: By the Qianlong reign Manchu and Mongol nurture-soldiers numbered more than twenty thousand three hundred.

sentences.zh: 盛京打牲烏拉，設總管、協領、佐領等員，轄打牲兵丁。

translations.literal: At Mukden's hunting ula, superintendents, assistant commanders, company commanders, and other officers were established to command hunting soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At Mukden's hunting ula, superintendents, assistant commanders, and company officers were appointed to oversee hunting troops.

sentences.zh: 吉林之參戶，蜜戶，漁戶，獵戶，鷹、狐、獺、鸛諸戶，咸隸內府三旗。

translations.literal: At Jilin the ginseng households, honey households, fishing households, hunting households, and eagle, fox, otter, and crane households—all were subordinate to the Imperial Household's three banners.
translations.idiomatic: At Jilin the ginseng, honey, fishing, and hunting households, along with eagle, fox, otter, and crane specialists, all fell under the Imperial Household's three banners.

sentences.zh: 其巡捕營汛守外七城門，上設步兵汛二十五所，城外分中南北三營，馬步兵汛額各有差，統以參將、游擊等。

translations.literal: Its patrol battalion garrisoned the seven outer city gates; above were twenty-five infantry posts; outside the city were divided central, south, and north camps—cavalry and infantry post quotas each differing—all commanded by brigadier generals, regimental commanders, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The patrol battalion guarded the seven outer gates; twenty-five infantry posts were established above, and outside the walls central, southern, and northern camps were formed, with varying cavalry and infantry strengths under brigadiers and regimental commanders.

sentences.zh: 暢春、圓明、靜明等園守兵，統以守備。

translations.literal: Guards for the Changchun, Yuanming, Jingming, and other gardens were commanded by garrison commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Guards for the Changchun, Old Summer Palace, Jingming, and other imperial gardens were commanded by garrison commandants.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，定駐蹕之地，八旗護軍分左右翼巡宿，啟蹕則三旗營總、護軍參領隨行。

translations.literal: In early Kangxi, encampment sites were fixed; Eight Banner guards were divided into left and right wings for patrol watch; when the procession set out, the three-banner camp commanders and guard brigade commanders accompanied.
translations.idiomatic: In early Kangxi encampment sites were designated; Eight Banner guards patrolled in left and right wings, and when the procession moved the three-banner camp commanders and guard brigade officers accompanied the emperor.

sentences.zh: 十三年，定八旗步兵二萬一千餘名，鳥槍步兵凡千七百三十七名。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Eight Banner infantry were fixed at more than twenty-one thousand men; musket infantry totaled one thousand seven hundred thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (1674) Eight Banner infantry were set at more than twenty-one thousand, including one thousand seven hundred thirty-seven musket infantry.

sentences.zh: 又定內九門外七門設城門校，轄十六門門軍。

translations.literal: It was further fixed that at the nine inner gates and seven outer gates gate captains were established, commanding gate troops at sixteen gates.
translations.idiomatic: Gate captains were also appointed for the nine inner and seven outer gates, commanding gate guards at sixteen gates in all.

sentences.zh: 其步軍營汛守皇城內各汛專用滿洲，城外各汛兼用蒙古、漢軍。

translations.literal: Its infantry brigade posts guarding posts within the Imperial City used only Manchu; posts outside the city used Mongol and Han Army together.
translations.idiomatic: The infantry brigade used only Manchu troops for posts within the Imperial City; outside the walls Mongol and Han bannermen served together.

sentences.zh: 尋定上駐園，則八旗兩翼，翼分七汛，更番宿衛。

translations.literal: Soon it was fixed that when the emperor resided at the gardens, the Eight Banners' two wings—each wing divided into seven posts—rotated in guard watch.
translations.idiomatic: It was soon ordered that when the emperor stayed at the gardens, the two banner wings—each divided into seven posts—would rotate palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 每日當值之前鋒、鳥槍護軍共七百二十人。

translations.literal: Daily on duty were seven hundred twenty vanguard and musket guards combined.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred twenty vanguard and musket guards were on daily duty.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，定田獵每年三舉，八旗各簡前鋒軍校以從。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, field hunts were fixed at three per year; each banner selected vanguard officers and sergeants to accompany.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (1682) three imperial hunts per year were mandated, with each banner selecting vanguard officers and sergeants to attend.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，定車駕巡幸期。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, the schedule for imperial carriage tours was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year (1683) the schedule for imperial progresses was fixed.

sentences.zh: 八旗驍騎營於內外城並增汛所。

translations.literal: The Eight Banners' vanguard cavalry brigade added posts in both inner and outer cities.
translations.idiomatic: The banner vanguard cavalry brigade added guard posts throughout the inner and outer cities.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以黑龍江所進精騎射、善殺虎者編虎槍營。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, skilled mounted archers and tiger-killers presented from Heilongjiang were organized into the Tiger Gun Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (1684) expert mounted archers and tiger hunters sent from Heilongjiang were formed into the Tiger Gun Battalion.

sentences.zh: 三十年，設火器營。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, the Firearms Battalion was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1691) the Firearms Battalion was established.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，設巡捕營，馬兵汛十五，步兵汛五十二。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, the Patrol Battalion was established—fifteen cavalry posts, fifty-two infantry posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng (1723) the Patrol Battalion was created with fifteen cavalry and fifty-two infantry posts.

sentences.zh: 凡朝會期，協尉、副尉率步軍巡警。

translations.literal: On all court assembly days, assistant marshals and deputy marshals led infantry in patrol policing.
translations.idiomatic: On days of court assembly, assistant and deputy marshals led infantry in patrol duty.

sentences.zh: 二年，諭各旗共選四千八百教養兵，習長槍挑刀各藝。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict ordered all banners jointly to select four thousand eight hundred nurture-and-training soldiers to practice long spear, pole sword, and other arts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1724) all banners were ordered to select four thousand eight hundred training soldiers to drill in long spear, pole sword, and related skills.

sentences.zh: 四年，令八旗前鋒習射，月六次。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Eight Banner vanguard were ordered to practice archery six times per month.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1726) banner vanguard were required to practice archery six times monthly.

sentences.zh: 其專司防火者曰防範兵。

translations.literal: Those exclusively charged with fire prevention were called precaution troops.
translations.idiomatic: Those assigned solely to fire prevention were called precaution troops.

sentences.zh: 九年，令五旗門汛護軍、馬甲均歸本營操演。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, guards and armored soldiers at the five banners' gate posts were ordered to return to their home camps for drill.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1731) gate guards and armored soldiers of the five lower banners were ordered back to their home camps for drill.

sentences.zh: 令三旗增訓練兵二千，編為二營。

translations.literal: The three banners were ordered to add two thousand training soldiers, organized into two battalions.
translations.idiomatic: The three upper banners were ordered to add two thousand training soldiers organized into two battalions.

sentences.zh: 十三年，額定馬甲五千二百五十，春秋二季合操。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, armored soldiers were fixed at five thousand two hundred fifty, with combined drill in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (1735) armored troops were fixed at five thousand two hundred fifty, with joint drills each spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十四年，設雲梯兵一營。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong, one cloud-ladder soldier battalion was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong (1749) a cloud-ladder (siege) battalion was established.

sentences.zh: 又於昆明湖設趕繒船，以前鋒軍習水戰。

translations.literal: Also at Kunming Lake dragnet boats were established, for the vanguard troops to practice naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Dragnet boats were also placed on Kunming Lake so the vanguard could drill in naval combat.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，令來京回人編一佐領，以和卓為佐領統轄之，後皆準此。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, an order was issued that Hui people who had come to the capital be organized into one company, with a khoja as company commander to command them—all later cases followed this.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong, Hui who had come to the capital were formed into a single company under a khoja company commander, a precedent followed thereafter.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，定大閱頭隊前鋒八旗，分為八隊，每隊小旗八，海螺四，為殿後兵。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, the grand review lead vanguard Eight Banners were fixed: divided into eight teams; each team had eight small banners and four conch shells, serving as rear-guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year of Qianlong the lead vanguard at the grand inspection was organized into eight teams of eight small banners and four conch horns each, serving as the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，以來京之番子視回人例，編一佐領，統於內務府正白旗。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, Tibetans who had come to the capital were treated by the Hui precedent, organized into one company, and placed under the Imperial Household Department's Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Qianlong, Tibetans newly arrived in the capital were registered in one company on the Hui model and assigned to the Imperial Household Department's Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，增京師步軍左右二營，合南北中為五營，分二十三汛，領兵一萬，於八旗漢軍鄂爾布、步甲、閒散內擇壯丁充補。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, the capital's left and right infantry camps were increased; together with the south, north, and central camps there were five camps, divided into twenty-three posts, commanding ten thousand troops—robust youths were selected from Han-banner erbo, infantry, and idle bannermen to fill the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year of Qianlong two left and right infantry battalions were added to the capital garrison, forming five camps with twenty-three posts and ten thousand troops drawn from Han-banner reserves, infantry soldiers, and idle bannermen.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，令巡捕五營以中營作提標，管圓明園五汛，參將四人，分管南北左右四營，共十八汛，兩翼總兵分轄之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, the five patrol camps were ordered to use the central camp as the brigade command post, managing five posts at the Old Summer Palace; four colonels separately managed the south, north, left, and right four camps—eighteen posts in all—with wing generals dividing jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiaqing the five patrol battalions were reorganized with the central battalion as brigade headquarters, five posts at the Old Summer Palace, and four colonels for the remaining camps covering eighteen posts under wing generals.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以增設之健銳營歸左翼，外火器營歸右翼，合八旗前鋒、內火器營、驍騎營凡三十六營。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the newly added Elite Sharp Vanguard Battalion was assigned to the left wing and the Outer Firearms Battalion to the right wing; together with the Eight Banner vanguard, Inner Firearms Battalion, and Cavalry Brigade there were thirty-six battalions in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Jiaqing the Elite Sharp Vanguard Battalion joined the left wing and the Outer Firearms Battalion the right wing, for thirty-six battalions in all counting vanguard, inner firearms, and cavalry forces.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，諭京師各旗營兵十四萬九千有奇，統兵大臣分班親閱，馬步火器，務令精整，不得以臨時召募濫充。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, an edict stated that capital garrison troops of the various banners numbered more than 149,000; ministers supervising troops were to inspect them in rotation; cavalry, infantry, and firearms must be kept in good order—temporary recruitment must not be used to fill ranks indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng the throne ordered that the capital's 149,000-odd banner garrison troops be inspected in rotation by supervising ministers, with cavalry, infantry, and firearms kept at full strength and no shoddy fill-ins from ad hoc recruitment.

sentences.zh: 十年，從勝保請，令八旗兵加練槍砲抬槍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, following Sheng Bao's request, Eight Banner troops were ordered to add training in muskets, cannon, and punt guns.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xianfeng, at Sheng Bao's request, banner troops were directed to add drill in muskets, cannon, and punt guns.

sentences.zh: 同治四年，諭醇親王訓練神機營，旗、綠各營，亦隨時校閱。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongzhi, an edict ordered Prince Chun to train the Shenji Battalion; banner and Green Standard camps were also to be inspected at intervals.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tongzhi Prince Chun was charged with training the Shenji Battalion, and banner and Green Standard units were to be inspected regularly.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十四年，選練神機營馬步隊，以萬人為先鋒隊，習槍砲及行陣戰法。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu, the Shenji Battalion's cavalry and infantry were selected and drilled; ten thousand men formed the vanguard, practicing firearms and battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu ten thousand Shenji cavalry and infantry were chosen as a vanguard and drilled in firearms and battlefield maneuvers.

sentences.zh: 此八旗兵衛制也。

translations.literal: This is the Eight Banner capital garrison system.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the system of Eight Banner troops guarding the capital.

sentences.zh: 八旗駐防之兵，大類有四：曰畿輔駐防兵，其籓部內附之眾，及在京內務府、理籓院所轄悉附焉；

translations.literal: Eight Banner garrison troops fell broadly into four categories: the metropolitan garrison troops—to which were attached peoples of submitted border domains, and all those under the Imperial Household Department and Court of Colonial Affairs in the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Garrison banner forces fell into four broad categories: metropolitan garrisons, which included submitted frontier peoples and troops under the Imperial Household Department and Court of Colonial Affairs in the capital;

sentences.zh: 曰東三省駐防兵；

translations.literal: the Three Eastern Provinces garrison troops;
translations.idiomatic: garrisons in the Three Eastern Provinces;

sentences.zh: 曰各直省駐防兵，新疆駐防兵附焉；

translations.literal: the provincial garrison troops, to which were attached the Xinjiang garrison troops;
translations.idiomatic: garrisons in the provinces, with Xinjiang garrisons counted among them;

sentences.zh: 曰籓部兵。

translations.literal: and border-domain troops.
translations.idiomatic: and frontier-domain troops.

sentences.zh: 畿輔駐防兵制，順治初，獨石口、張家口、山海關、喜峰口、古北口並設防禦一人或二人，采育里、固安縣設防守尉、防禦有差。

translations.literal: The metropolitan garrison system: at the beginning of Shunzhi, at Dushikou, Zhangjiakou, Shanhaiguan, Xifengkou, and Gubeikou defensive officers were established, one or two each; at Caiyuli and Gu'an County defense captains and defensive officers were established in varying numbers.
translations.idiomatic: For metropolitan garrisons, early Shunzhi saw defensive officers posted one or two at a time at Dushikou, Zhangjiakou, Shanhaiguan, Xifengkou, and Gubeikou, while Caiyuli and Gu'an County received defense captains and defensive officers in varying numbers.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年，察哈爾八旗，每旗設總管一人，副總管一人，參領三人，佐領、驍騎校、護軍校各有差。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi, for the Chahar Eight Banners each banner had one superintendent, one deputy superintendent, three brigade commanders, and company commanders, cavalry captains, and guard captains in varying numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi each Chahar banner was given one superintendent, one deputy superintendent, three brigade commanders, and varying numbers of company commanders, cavalry captains, and guard captains.

sentences.zh: 捕盜官每旗二人，親軍、前鋒各二，護軍十七，領催四，驍騎二十五。

translations.literal: Each banner had two bandit-capture officers, two personal guards and two vanguard each, seventeen guards, four squad leaders, and twenty-five cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Each banner had two bandit-capture officers, two personal guards and two vanguard soldiers, seventeen guards, four squad leaders, and twenty-five cavalry.

sentences.zh: 在京蒙古都統兼轄之。

translations.literal: They were jointly commanded by the Mongol commander-in-chief in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They were placed under the joint command of the Mongol banner commander in the capital.

sentences.zh: 山海關總管一人，防禦八人，滿、蒙、漢兵七百有奇。

translations.literal: At Shanhaiguan there was one superintendent, eight defensive officers, and more than seven hundred Manchu, Mongol, and Han troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shanhaiguan had one superintendent, eight defensive officers, and over seven hundred Manchu, Mongol, and Han soldiers.

sentences.zh: 尋設張家口總管一，防禦七，兵百三十有奇。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward a Zhangjiakou superintendent was established, with seven defensive officers and more than 130 troops.
translations.idiomatic: A Zhangjiakou superintendent was soon added with seven defensive officers and over 130 troops.

sentences.zh: 獨石口、古北口增防禦各二，喜峰口防禦二，冷口、羅文峪防禦各一，兵多則六十八，少則十二人。

translations.literal: At Dushikou and Gubeikou two defensive officers were added each; at Xifengkou two defensive officers; at Lengkou and Luowenyu one defensive officer each—troops numbered as many as sixty-eight or as few as twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Dushikou and Gubeikou each gained two defensive officers, Xifengkou two, and Lengkou and Luowenyu one apiece, with garrisons ranging from twelve to sixty-eight men.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，設天津水師營都統一，協領六，佐領、防禦、驍騎校各三十二，旗兵千六百人，蒙古兵四百人，分左右兩翼。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng, one naval commander was established at the Tianjin Naval Brigade, with six assistant commanders, thirty-two company commanders, defensive officers, and cavalry captains each, 1,600 banner troops and 400 Mongol troops, divided into left and right wings.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongzheng the Tianjin Naval Brigade received one commander, six assistant commanders, thirty-two each of company commanders, defensive officers, and cavalry captains, 1,600 banner troops and 400 Mongols in left and right wings.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，增熱河駐防兵二千人，委前鋒校、前鋒、領催、鳥槍領催、馬甲、鳥槍馬甲、砲甲、弓矢匠各有差，以千四百人駐熱河，四百駐喀喇河屯、二百駐樺榆溝。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong, 2,000 Rehe garrison troops were added, with vanguard sergeants, vanguard, squad leaders, musket squad leaders, armored soldiers, musket armored soldiers, artillery soldiers, and bow-and-arrow craftsmen assigned in varying numbers—1,400 garrisoned at Rehe, 400 at Kalahetun, and 200 at Huayugou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianlong 2,000 Rehe garrison troops were added with vanguard sergeants, squad leaders, musket troops, armored soldiers, artillerymen, and bow craftsmen in set numbers, 1,400 at Rehe, 400 at Kalahetun, and 200 at Huayugou.

sentences.zh: 八年，改山海關總管為副都統，增協領、佐領諸屬，滿、蒙、漢兵共八百人，分左右翼。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Shanhaiguan superintendent was changed to a deputy commander-in-chief; assistant commanders, company commanders, and other subordinates were added; Manchu, Mongol, and Han troops totaled eight hundred, divided into left and right wings.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Qianlong the Shanhaiguan superintendent became a deputy commander-in-chief with added assistant commanders and company officers, 800 Manchu, Mongol, and Han troops in left and right wings.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，設察哈爾都統一人，駐張家口，理八旗游牧，兼轄防兵，副都統二人，駐左右翼游牧邊界。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, one Chahar commander-in-chief was established, garrisoned at Zhangjiakou, managing Eight Banner nomadic affairs and also commanding garrison troops; two deputy commanders-in-chief were garrisoned at the left and right wing nomadic frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Qianlong one Chahar commander was posted at Zhangjiakou to oversee banner nomads and garrison troops, with two deputy commanders on the left and right nomadic frontiers.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，設駐防密雲滿、蒙兵二千。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, 2,000 Manchu and Mongol garrison troops were established at Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong 2,000 Manchu and Mongol troops were posted at Miyun.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，增熱河圍場副都統。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing, a deputy commander-in-chief for the Rehe hunting preserve was added.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiaqing a deputy commander was added for the Rehe hunting preserve.

sentences.zh: 九年，改總管。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the post was changed to superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Jiaqing the office was redesignated superintendent.

sentences.zh: 十五年，改設都統一人。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, one commander-in-chief was established in place of the former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Jiaqing the post was again changed to a single commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 以厄魯特達什達瓦降眾徙居科布多，旋分其屬為三旗，設總管、副總管、佐領、驍騎校等。

translations.literal: The surrendered Oirat followers of Dashdava were relocated to Kobdo; shortly afterward their followers were divided into three banners, with superintendents, deputy superintendents, company commanders, cavalry captains, and the like established.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered Oirat followers of Dashdava were resettled at Kobdo and soon organized into three banners with superintendents, deputy superintendents, company commanders, and cavalry captains.

sentences.zh: 尋移至熱河，作為官兵。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward they were moved to Rehe and made regular officers and troops.
translations.idiomatic: They were soon transferred to Rehe and incorporated as regular garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 先是康熙中，建避暑山莊於熱河，設總管、守備、千總分守各行宮。

translations.literal: Previously in the Kangxi period, the Mountain Resort for Escaping the Heat was built at Rehe; superintendents, garrison commanders, and platoon leaders were established to guard the various palaces separately.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in the Kangxi reign the Mountain Resort was built at Rehe, with superintendents, garrison commanders, and platoon leaders assigned to guard each palace compound.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，增建行宮，設千總、委署千總一二人，兵自六人至九十八人不等。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong period, additional palaces were built; platoon leaders and acting platoon leaders, one or two each, were established; troops ranged from six to ninety-eight men.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong more palace compounds were added, each with one or two platoon leaders or acting platoon leaders and garrisons of six to ninety-eight men.

sentences.zh: 木蘭圍場總管一人。

translations.literal: The Mulan hunting preserve had one superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: The Mulan hunting preserve had one superintendent.

sentences.zh: 康熙季年，設有防禦八及滿、蒙兵百餘。

translations.literal: In the late Kangxi period, eight defensive officers and more than one hundred Manchu and Mongol troops were established.
translations.idiomatic: In late Kangxi eight defensive officers and over one hundred Manchu and Mongol troops were posted there.

sentences.zh: 迨乾隆中年，增左右翼長二，驍騎校八，駐兵共八百人。

translations.literal: By the middle of the Qianlong period, two left and right wing chiefs, eight cavalry captains, and eight hundred garrison troops in all were added.
translations.idiomatic: By mid-Qianlong two wing chiefs and eight cavalry captains had been added, with 800 garrison troops in all.

sentences.zh: 每一兵給地一頃二十畝，或地不宜耕種，則改給牛羊。

translations.literal: Each soldier was granted 1.2 qing of land; if the land was unsuitable for cultivation, cattle and sheep were given instead.
translations.idiomatic: Each soldier received 1.2 qing of land, or cattle and sheep where the soil was unsuitable for farming.

sentences.zh: 木蘭之地，周遭樹柵為界，設營房八，卡倫四十，八旗各分五卡倫，各以旗兵守之。

translations.literal: The Mulan grounds were bounded by palisades all around; eight barracks and forty karun outposts were established—the Eight Banners each assigned five karun, each guarded by its own banner troops.
translations.idiomatic: Mulan was enclosed by a palisade fence with eight barracks and forty karun outposts, five per banner, each manned by its own troops.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，諭駐京旗兵，遇閏月賞給甲米，他省不得援例。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang, an edict stated that capital garrison banner troops, when a leap month occurred, were to be granted armor-ration grain as a reward—other provinces must not cite this as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daoguang the throne granted capital garrison troops extra grain rations in leap months, a privilege not extended to other provinces.

sentences.zh: 此畿輔駐防制也。

translations.literal: This is the metropolitan garrison system.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the metropolitan garrison system.

sentences.zh: 東三省駐防兵制，共駐四十四所，兵三萬五千三百餘人。

translations.literal: The Three Eastern Provinces garrison system: garrisons totaled forty-four posts, with more than 35,300 troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Eastern Provinces had forty-four garrison posts and more than 35,300 troops.

sentences.zh: 凡前鋒、領催、馬甲、守門庫等兵，步甲、夜捕手、匠役、養育兵、鳥槍馬甲、領催、水手之屬，或設或否，名額多寡，各視駐地所宜，損益區置之，初無定限。

translations.literal: As for vanguard, squad leader, armored soldier, gate-and-storehouse guard, and other troops; infantry, night patrolmen, craftsmen, training soldiers, musket armored soldiers, squad leaders, sailors, and the like—whether established or not, and how many quotas, all depended on what each garrison post required, adjusted by increase or decrease; there was no fixed limit at the outset.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard, squad leaders, armored soldiers, gate guards, infantry, night patrolmen, craftsmen, training soldiers, musket troops, and sailors were assigned as each post required, with no fixed quotas at first.

sentences.zh: 其在盛京，天聰間始設駐防於牛庄、蓋州，兵九十六人。

translations.literal: At Mukden, during the Tiancong period garrisons were first established at Niuzhuang and Gaizhou, with ninety-six troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Mukden the first garrisons, at Niuzhuang and Gaizhou with ninety-six men, date to the Tiancong period.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，世祖將遷燕京，設盛京八旗駐防兵，以正黃旗內大臣和洛會總統之，以鑲黃旗梅勒章京統左翼，正紅旗梅勒章京統右翼。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, as the Founding Emperor was about to move the capital to Yanjing, Mukden Eight Banner garrison troops were established; the Plain Yellow Banner grand minister Hooge was made overall commander; the Bordered Yellow Banner meiren janggin commanded the left wing, and the Plain Red Banner meiren janggin the right wing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi, as the emperor prepared to move the capital to Yanjing, Mukden Eight Banner garrisons were established under Hooge of the Plain Yellow Banner, with meiren janggin commanding the left and right wings.

sentences.zh: 每旗設滿洲協領一，佐領四，蒙古、漢軍佐領各一。

translations.literal: Each banner had one Manchu assistant commander, four company commanders, and one Mongol and one Han Army company commander each.
translations.idiomatic: Each banner had one Manchu assistant commander, four company commanders, and one Mongol and one Han company commander apiece.

sentences.zh: 設熊岳城守官，其下滿洲佐領三，漢軍佐領一，錦州、鳳凰城、寧遠城守官，其下各設滿洲佐領各二，漢軍佐領一，興京、遼陽、牛庄、岫岩、義州城守官，滿洲佐領各一人，蓋州、海州滿、漢佐領各一，統駐防兵。

translations.literal: Garrison commanders were established at Xiongyue City, with three Manchu company commanders and one Han Army company commander beneath; at Jinzhou, Fenghuangcheng, and Ningyuan garrison commanders were established, each with two Manchu company commanders and one Han Army company commander; at Xingjing, Liaoyang, Niuzhuang, Xiuyan, and Yizhou garrison commanders had one Manchu company commander each; at Gaizhou and Haizhou one Manchu and one Han company commander each—all commanding garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commanders were posted at Xiongyue, Jinzhou, Fenghuangcheng, Ningyuan, Xingjing, Liaoyang, Niuzhuang, Xiuyan, Yizhou, Gaizhou, and Haizhou, each with Manchu and Han company commanders as needed, all commanding local garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，改盛京昂邦章京為鎮守遼東等處將軍，梅勒章京二人為副都統，統轄協領、佐領、驍騎校。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, the Mukden angbang janggin was changed to General Garrisoning Liaodong and Other Places; two meiren janggin became deputy commanders-in-chief, commanding assistant commanders, company commanders, and cavalry captains.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi the Mukden angbang janggin became the General Garrisoning Liaodong, with two meiren janggin as deputy commanders overseeing assistant commanders, company commanders, and cavalry captains.

sentences.zh: 四年，改遼東將軍為奉天將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Liaodong General was renamed the Fengtian General.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kangxi the Liaodong General was retitled the Fengtian General.

sentences.zh: 十四年，設錦州、義州城守尉各一，佐領、驍騎校各有差。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, one garrison captain each was established at Jinzhou and Yizhou, with company commanders and cavalry captains in varying numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi garrison captains were posted at Jinzhou and Yizhou with company commanders and cavalry captains in set numbers.

sentences.zh: 各邊門皆置防禦一。

translations.literal: At each frontier gate one defensive officer was posted.
translations.idiomatic: Each frontier gate received one defensive officer.

sentences.zh: 尋設開原防禦三，金州防禦一，兵弁各有差。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward three defensive officers were established at Kaiyuan and one at Jinzhou; officers and troops were assigned in varying numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Three defensive officers were soon added at Kaiyuan and one at Jinzhou, with officers and troops assigned as needed.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，設金州駐防水師營，船十號，兵五百，水手一百。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, a Jinzhou garrison naval brigade was established, with ten vessels, five hundred troops, and one hundred sailors.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year of Kangxi a naval brigade was posted at Jinzhou with ten vessels, 500 troops, and 100 sailors.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，設熊岳副都統一人，廣寧、義州、錦州、寧遠至山海關設副都統一，復州、南金州、鳳凰城、岫岩、旅順等處設副都統一，分轄旗兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, one Xiongyue deputy commander-in-chief was established; one deputy commander-in-chief was established from Guangning, Yizhou, Jinzhou, and Ningyuan to Shanhaiguan; one deputy commander-in-chief was established at Fuzhou, Nanjinzhou, Fenghuangcheng, Xiuyan, Lüshun, and other places—dividing jurisdiction over banner troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongzheng one deputy commander was posted at Xiongyue, another from Guangning through Jinzhou and Ningyuan to Shanhaiguan, and a third at Fuzhou, Nanjinzhou, Fenghuangcheng, Xiuyan, Lüshun, and nearby posts to divide command of banner troops.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十二年，改奉天將軍為鎮守盛京將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Qianlong, the Fengtian General was renamed the General Garrisoning Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Qianlong the Fengtian General was retitled General Garrisoning Mukden.

sentences.zh: 盛京各額兵都一萬五千有奇。

translations.literal: Mukden's quota troops in all numbered more than 15,000.
translations.idiomatic: Mukden's authorized strength totaled more than 15,000 troops.

sentences.zh: 其在吉林，順治十年，設寧古塔昂邦章京一，梅勒章京二，佐領、驍騎校各八。

translations.literal: At Jilin, in the tenth year of Shunzhi one Ningguta angbang janggin, two meiren janggin, and eight company commanders and cavalry captains each were established.
translations.idiomatic: At Jilin, in the tenth year of Shunzhi Ningguta received one angbang janggin, two meiren janggin, and eight company commanders and cavalry captains each.

sentences.zh: 十八年，設吉林水師營。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, the Jilin Naval Brigade was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Shunzhi the Jilin Naval Brigade was established.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，改寧古塔昂邦章京為將軍，梅勒章京為副都統。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, the Ningguta angbang janggin was changed to general, and the meiren janggin to deputy commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi the Ningguta angbang janggin became a general and the meiren janggin a deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 三年，設水師營總管各員。

translations.literal: In the third year, naval brigade superintendents and other officers were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kangxi superintendents were appointed for the naval brigade.

sentences.zh: 七年，增寧古塔協領二。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, two Ningguta assistant commanders were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kangxi two assistant commanders were added at Ningguta.

sentences.zh: 十年，以寧古塔副都統一，佐領、驍騎校各十一，兵七百，移駐吉林。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, one Ningguta deputy commander-in-chief, eleven company commanders and cavalry captains each, and seven hundred troops were moved to garrison Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Kangxi one Ningguta deputy commander with eleven company commanders and cavalry captains and 700 troops relocated to Jilin.

sentences.zh: 又增吉林協領八，佐領、防禦、驍騎校各十二，兵六百人。

translations.literal: Eight Jilin assistant commanders were also added, with twelve company commanders, defensive officers, and cavalry captains each, and six hundred troops.
translations.idiomatic: Eight more assistant commanders were added at Jilin with twelve each of company commanders, defensive officers, and cavalry captains and 600 troops.

sentences.zh: 尋增防禦十五人。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward fifteen defensive officers were added.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen defensive officers were soon added.

sentences.zh: 十五年，移寧古塔將軍駐吉林，留副都統於寧古塔，增吉林副都統一人。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, the Ningguta general was moved to garrison Jilin; a deputy commander-in-chief was left at Ningguta, and one Jilin deputy commander-in-chief was added.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi the Ningguta general moved to Jilin, leaving a deputy commander at Ningguta and adding one at Jilin.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，設伯都訥協領二人，佐領、驍騎校各三十，防禦八。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, two Boduna assistant commanders were established, with thirty company commanders and cavalry captains each, and eight defensive officers.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year of Kangxi Boduna received two assistant commanders, thirty company commanders and cavalry captains each, and eight defensive officers.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，設三姓、琿春協領一，佐領、驍騎校、防禦有差。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year, one assistant commander each was established at Sanxing and Hunchun, with company commanders, cavalry captains, and defensive officers in varying numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year of Kangxi Sanxing and Hunchun each gained an assistant commander with company commanders, cavalry captains, and defensive officers as needed.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，設阿勒楚喀協領一人，佐領、驍騎校、防禦各五。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng, one Aletukai assistant commander was established, with five company commanders, cavalry captains, and defensive officers each.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongzheng Aletukai received one assistant commander and five each of company commanders, cavalry captains, and defensive officers.

sentences.zh: 十年，設三姓副都統一人。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, one Sanxing deputy commander-in-chief was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yongzheng one deputy commander was posted at Sanxing.

sentences.zh: 尋設吉林鳥槍營參領一人，佐領、驍騎校各八，鳥槍兵千。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward one Jilin Musket Battalion brigade commander was established, with eight company commanders and cavalry captains each, and one thousand musket troops.
translations.idiomatic: A Jilin Musket Battalion was soon added with one brigade commander, eight company commanders and cavalry captains, and 1,000 musket troops.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年，令打牲烏拉兵歸吉林將軍兼轄。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong, the hunting ula troops were ordered to come under the joint command of the Jilin general.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong the hunting ula corps was placed under the Jilin general's joint command.

sentences.zh: 先是順治時，設打牲烏拉協領二，又設總管一人，統轄珠軒頭目，及參、蜜、漁、獵諸戶，專司采捕諸役。

translations.literal: Previously in the Shunzhi period, two hunting ula assistant commanders were established, and one superintendent was also established, commanding pearl-tribute convoy chiefs and ginseng, honey, fishing, and hunting households, specializing in collection and hunting duties.
translations.idiomatic: As early as Shunzhi two hunting ula assistant commanders and one superintendent had been appointed to oversee pearl convoys and ginseng, honey, fishing, and hunting households devoted to tribute collection.

sentences.zh: 後遞增佐領、防禦八，驍騎校十或八，額兵千。

translations.literal: Later company commanders and defensive officers were added in succession to eight, cavalry captains to ten or eight, and quota troops to one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Over time the corps grew to eight company commanders and defensive officers, ten or eight cavalry captains, and 1,000 authorized troops.

sentences.zh: 至是以在吉林境，命兼統于吉林將軍。

translations.literal: At this point, because they were within Jilin territory, an order was issued that they be jointly commanded by the Jilin general.
translations.idiomatic: Because the corps lay within Jilin, it was now ordered under the Jilin general's joint command.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，設阿勒楚喀副都統一人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, one Aletukai deputy commander-in-chief was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Qianlong one deputy commander was posted at Aletukai.

sentences.zh: 道光六年，以雙城堡移駐京旗分左右翼，各設總、副屯達二人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang, capital banner troops relocated to Shuangchengbo were divided into left and right wings, each with two chief and deputy colony overseers.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daoguang capital banner colonists at Shuangchengbo were split into left and right wings, each with two chief and deputy colony overseers.

sentences.zh: 嗣又分一旗五屯，增總、副屯達各六人。

translations.literal: Later one banner was further divided into five colonies, and six chief and six deputy colony overseers were added.
translations.idiomatic: Later one banner was subdivided into five colonies and six chief and six deputy colony overseers were added.

sentences.zh: 其在黑龍江，當康熙初年，自吉林移水師營來駐齊齊哈爾等處，水手一千有奇。

translations.literal: At Heilongjiang, in the early Kangxi period, the naval brigade was moved from Jilin to garrison Qiqihar and other places, with more than one thousand sailors.
translations.idiomatic: In Heilongjiang, early in the Kangxi reign the naval brigade was transferred from Jilin to Qiqihar and nearby posts with over 1,000 sailors.

sentences.zh: 盛京壯丁散處者，隨時編入八旗。

translations.literal: Robust youths scattered in Mukden were enrolled into the Eight Banners as occasion arose.
translations.idiomatic: Able-bodied youths scattered across Mukden were enrolled in the banners as needed.

sentences.zh: 巴爾呼人、錫伯人居近吉林，卦勒察人居近伯都訥，庫爾喀人居近琿春，並設佐領、驍騎校等分駐。

translations.literal: Barhu and Xibe people lived near Jilin; Guwalgiya people lived near Boduna; Kurka people lived near Hunchun—company commanders, cavalry captains, and the like were established and garrisoned separately.
translations.idiomatic: Barhu and Xibe were settled near Jilin, Guwalgiya near Boduna, and Kurka near Hunchun, each with company commanders and cavalry captains posted separately.

sentences.zh: 其東北最遠者，索倫、達呼爾二部，天命、天聰間，相率內附，其後分充各城額兵。

translations.literal: Farthest to the northeast were the Solon and Daur two groups; during the Tianming and Tiancong periods they submitted in succession, and afterward were distributed to fill quota troops at the various garrison cities.
translations.idiomatic: Farthest northeast were the Solon and Daur, who submitted during the Tianming and Tiancong reigns and were later distributed as quota troops among the garrison cities.

sentences.zh: 至鄂倫春所居益遠，使馬、使鹿部分處山林，業捕貂，皆審戶比丁，列于軍伍。

translations.literal: The Oroqen lived even farther; the horse-using and deer-using groups dwelt separately in mountain forests, making their living hunting sable—all households were reviewed and males counted, and they were enrolled in the military rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The Oroqen lived still farther out; horse-using and deer-using bands in the forests hunted sable for a living, and all households were registered and their men listed in the military rolls.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，初置黑龍江將軍，原水師營總管等並屬之，設副都統二，協領四，佐領、驍騎校各二十四，防禦八，滿洲兵千，索倫、達呼爾兵五百，駐愛琿城。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, the Heilongjiang general was first established; the former naval brigade superintendent and others all came under his command; two deputy commanders-in-chief, four assistant commanders, twenty-four company commanders and cavalry captains each, and eight defensive officers were established; one thousand Manchu troops and five hundred Solon and Daur troops garrisoned Aihui City.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Kangxi the first Heilongjiang general was appointed, absorbing the naval superintendent and staff, with two deputy commanders, four assistant commanders, twenty-four company commanders and cavalry captains, eight defensive officers, 1,000 Manchu and 500 Solon and Daur troops at Aihui.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，設打牲處總管一，副總管二，以索倫、達呼爾壯丁編設佐領、驍騎校。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, one hunting superintendent and two deputy superintendents were established; Solon and Daur robust youths were organized to establish company commanders and cavalry captains.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Kangxi one hunting superintendent and two deputies were appointed, with Solon and Daur youths organized into company commanders and cavalry captains.

sentences.zh: 尋於墨爾根城設駐防兵。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward garrison troops were established at Moergen City.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison troops were soon posted at Moergen.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，移將軍駐墨爾根，又增協領四，佐領、驍騎校各七，索倫、達呼爾兵四百餘，以副都統一人統兵駐愛琿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the general was moved to garrison Moergen; four assistant commanders were also added, seven company commanders and cavalry captains each, and more than four hundred Solon and Daur troops; one deputy commander-in-chief commanded troops garrisoned at Aihui.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi the general moved to Moergen with four more assistant commanders, seven company commanders and cavalry captains, and 400-odd Solon and Daur troops, while one deputy commander remained at Aihui.

sentences.zh: 尋設兵千餘駐防齊齊哈爾。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward more than one thousand troops were established to garrison Qiqihar.
translations.idiomatic: More than 1,000 troops were soon posted at Qiqihar.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，將軍復自墨爾根移駐齊齊哈爾。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, the general again moved from Moergen to garrison Qiqihar.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi the general returned from Moergen to Qiqihar.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，設墨爾根副都統一人。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, one Moergen deputy commander-in-chief was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year of Kangxi one deputy commander was posted at Moergen.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，增設打牲處總管三，滿洲、索倫、達呼爾副總管十六，索倫、達呼爾佐領、驍騎校各六十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng, three hunting superintendents were added, sixteen Manchu, Solon, and Daur deputy superintendents, and sixty-two Solon and Daur company commanders and cavalry captains each.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongzheng three hunting superintendents, sixteen Manchu, Solon, and Daur deputy superintendents, and sixty-two Solon and Daur company commanders and cavalry captains were added.

sentences.zh: 十年，設呼倫貝爾統領一，索倫、巴爾呼總管、副總管各二，佐領、驍騎校各五十，兵三千，尋增兵二千有奇。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, one Hulun Buir commander was established, two Solon and Barhu superintendents and deputy superintendents each, fifty company commanders and cavalry captains each, and three thousand troops; shortly afterward more than two thousand troops were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yongzheng one Hulun Buir commander was appointed with two Solon and Barhu superintendents and deputies each, fifty company commanders and cavalry captains, 3,000 troops, and soon over 2,000 more.

sentences.zh: 厄魯特總管、副總管各一。

translations.literal: One Oirat superintendent and one deputy superintendent were also established.
translations.idiomatic: One Oirat superintendent and one deputy were also appointed.

sentences.zh: 乾隆八年，改呼倫貝爾統領為副都統。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qianlong, the Hulun Buir commander was changed to deputy commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Qianlong the Hulun Buir commander was retitled deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶九年，以齊齊哈爾等處承種官田馬甲歸各本旗，所墾新田，改增養育兵耕種。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiaqing, armored soldiers who had cultivated official fields at Qiqihar and other places were returned to their original banners; newly reclaimed land was changed so that training soldiers would cultivate it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Jiaqing armored soldiers farming official land at Qiqihar and elsewhere reverted to their home banners, and newly reclaimed fields were assigned to training soldiers for cultivation.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年，增黑龍江馬甲千。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng, one thousand Heilongjiang armored soldiers were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xianfeng 1,000 armored soldiers were added to the Heilongjiang garrison.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，將軍文緒請由黑省至茂興設七站，由茂興至呼蘭設五台，共台站六十人，置掌路記防禦一，驍騎校二，領催六，分隸鈐束。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu, General Wenzu requested that seven relay stations be established from Heilongjiang province to Maoxing, and five stations from Maoxing to Hulan—sixty relay personnel in all—with one route-record defensive officer, two cavalry captains, and six squad leaders established, each subordinate under separate supervision.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Guangxu General Wenzu proposed seven relay stations from Heilongjiang to Maoxing and five from Maoxing to Hulan, 60 relay personnel in all, with one route-record defensive officer, two cavalry captains, and six squad leaders under divided command.

sentences.zh: 黑龍江八旗兵約分五類：曰前鋒，共百四十六人，佩橐鞬，負旗幟，為先導；

translations.literal: Heilongjiang Eight Banner troops fell roughly into five categories: vanguard, 146 in all, wearing quivers and sword-belts, bearing flags and banners, serving as guides;
translations.idiomatic: Heilongjiang banner troops fell into five broad categories: vanguard, 146 in all, wearing quivers and sword-belts and bearing flags as guides;

sentences.zh: 曰領催，供會計書寫，馬甲之長也，共七百四十八人；

translations.literal: squad leaders, who handled accounts and writing and were heads of the armored soldiers, 748 in all;
translations.idiomatic: squad leaders who kept accounts and records and headed the armored soldiers, 748 in all;

sentences.zh: 曰馬甲，又稱披甲，共九千二百十三人；

translations.literal: armored soldiers, also called mail-clad troops, 9,213 in all;
translations.idiomatic: armored soldiers, also called mail-clad troops, 9,213 in all;

sentences.zh: 曰匠役，為鳥槍、弓、鐵、鞍諸匠，共一百五十二人；

translations.literal: Called artisans—musket-makers, bowyers, ironworkers, and saddlers, 152 in all;
translations.idiomatic: Next came the artisans: musket-makers, bowyers, smiths, and saddlers, 152 in all.

sentences.zh: 曰養育兵，康熙季年，始以旗兵屯田，至嘉慶中，改屯田馬甲為養育兵，共八百人。

translations.literal: Called training soldiers—in the closing years of Kangxi, banner troops first undertook tuntian; by the Jiaqing period, tuntian armored soldiers were changed to training soldiers, 800 in all.
translations.idiomatic: Training soldiers: in the late Kangxi period banner troops first took up military colonization, and by the Jiaqing reign tuntian armored soldiers were reclassified as training soldiers, 800 in all.

sentences.zh: 別有未入伍者曰西丹，譯言控馬奴，不得預征伐之事。

translations.literal: Separately, those not enlisted in the ranks were called xidan, which means horse-handling slaves; they might not participate in campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Those not yet enrolled in the ranks were called xidan, meaning horse-handlers; they were barred from military campaigns.

sentences.zh: 此東三省駐防制也。

translations.literal: This was the garrison system of the Three Eastern Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the garrison system of the Three Eastern Provinces.

sentences.zh: 各直省駐防制，順治二年，始設江南江寧左翼四旗，陝西西安右翼四旗，皆置滿、蒙兵二千，弓匠二十八，鐵匠五十六。

translations.literal: As for the garrison system in the various provinces, in the second year of Shunzhi the Left Wing Four Banners at Jiangning in Jiangnan and the Right Wing Four Banners at Xi'an in Shaanxi were first established, each with 2,000 Manchu and Mongol troops, 28 bow artisans, and 56 iron artisans.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial garrison system began in the second year of Shunzhi with the Left Wing Four Banners at Jiangning and the Right Wing Four Banners at Xi'an, each staffed with 2,000 Manchu and Mongol troops, 28 bowyers, and 56 smiths.

sentences.zh: 六年，于山西太原設正藍、鑲藍二旗滿、蒙駐防兵，暨游牧察哈爾兵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, at Taiyuan in Shanxi, garrison troops of the Plain Blue and Bordered Blue banners—Manchu and Mongol—and nomadic Chahar troops were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year garrison troops of the Plain Blue and Bordered Blue banners were placed at Taiyuan in Shanxi, together with nomadic Chahar troops.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗親征察哈爾，降土默特之眾，後編為二旗，設左右翼，都統部眾得同辦事。

translations.literal: At first, Taizong personally campaigned against the Chahar and reduced the Tumed people; afterward they were organized into two banners with left and right wings, and their banner generals could conduct affairs jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Taizong had campaigned in person against the Chahar and subdued the Tumed; they were later organized into two banners with left and right wings, their banner generals holding joint authority.

sentences.zh: 旋裁都統，以旗務掌之將軍、副都統，與內八旗等。

translations.literal: Soon the banner generals were abolished, and the general and deputy commanders-in-chief who managed banner affairs were made equal to the Inner Eight Banners.
translations.idiomatic: The banner general posts were soon abolished, and the generals and deputy commanders who managed banner affairs were placed on the same footing as the Inner Eight Banners.

sentences.zh: 至是，游牧察哈爾遂列于山西駐防。

translations.literal: At this point, the nomadic Chahar were listed among the Shanxi garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: The nomadic Chahar were henceforth assigned to the Shanxi garrison.

sentences.zh: 十一年，設山東德州鑲黃、正黃二旗滿、蒙領催、馬甲暨弓、鐵匠。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, at Dezhou in Shandong, the Bordered Yellow and Plain Yellow banners' Manchu and Mongol squad leaders, armored soldiers, and bow and iron artisans were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Bordered Yellow and Plain Yellow banners placed Manchu and Mongol squad leaders, armored cavalry, and bowyers and smiths at Dezhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 十五年，增設西安佐領、驍騎校二十八，驍騎一千。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, 28 company commanders and cavalry captains and 1,000 elite cavalry were added at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Xi'an received 28 company commanders and cavalry captains and 1,000 elite cavalry.

sentences.zh: 設浙江杭州滿、蒙八旗馬甲、步甲、弓匠，漢軍馬甲、步甲、鐵匠，滿、漢棉甲兵，共四千有奇。

translations.literal: At Hangzhou in Zhejiang, Manchu and Mongol Eight Banner armored cavalry, foot soldiers, and bow artisans, Han Banner armored cavalry, foot soldiers, and iron artisans, and Manchu and Han cotton-armor troops were established, more than 4,000 in all.
translations.idiomatic: At Hangzhou in Zhejiang the garrison was staffed with Manchu and Mongol banner armored cavalry, foot soldiers, and bowyers; Han banner armored cavalry, foot soldiers, and smiths; and Manchu and Han cotton-armor troops—more than 4,000 in all.

sentences.zh: 其後每旗並增佐領、驍騎校、驍騎。

translations.literal: Thereafter each banner also had company commanders, cavalry captains, and elite cavalry added.
translations.idiomatic: Each banner thereafter received additional company commanders, cavalry captains, and elite cavalry.

sentences.zh: 十六年，改設京口駐防鎮海將軍一，副都統二，協領、參領、防禦、佐領、驍騎校有差。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the garrison at Jingkou was reorganized with one Zhenhai general, two deputy commanders-in-chief, and assorted assistant commanders, regimental commanders, defensive officers, company commanders, and cavalry captains.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the Jingkou garrison was reorganized under one Zhenhai general and two deputy commanders-in-chief, with assistant commanders, regimental commanders, defensive officers, company commanders, and cavalry captains in fixed numbers.

sentences.zh: 尋增江寧、西安步甲各一千。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, 1,000 foot soldiers each were added at Jiangning and Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangning and Xi'an each soon received 1,000 additional foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，增西安右翼四旗滿、蒙馬甲千，弓、鐵匠十四，漢軍馬甲等，江寧馬甲千。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, 1,000 Manchu and Mongol armored soldiers, 14 bow and iron artisans, Han Banner armored soldiers, and the like were added to the Right Wing Four Banners at Xi'an; 1,000 armored soldiers were added at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi Xi'an's Right Wing Four Banners gained 1,000 Manchu and Mongol armored cavalry, 14 bowyers and smiths, and Han banner armored soldiers; Jiangning gained 1,000 armored cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後又各增兵二千及弓、鐵匠等。

translations.literal: Afterward 2,000 troops each and bow and iron artisans and the like were added again.
translations.idiomatic: Each garrison later received another 2,000 troops plus bowyers, smiths, and the like.

sentences.zh: 是年增京口步甲千人。

translations.literal: That year 1,000 foot soldiers were added at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Jingkou received 1,000 foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 十五年，設陝西寧夏八旗滿、蒙領催，馬甲，步甲，弓、鐵匠。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, at Ningxia in Shaanxi, Eight Banner Manchu and Mongol squad leaders, armored soldiers, foot soldiers, and bow and iron artisans were established.
